MC	<p>175d_d982</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene J</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #59651b;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #59651b;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #59651b;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jwy, +++, jwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene F</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276198;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f3876;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cfp, +++, cfp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7088_a9ee</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cey, +++, cey"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>27de_9480</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene N</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ajn, +++, ajn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dry, +++, dry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>277c_1584</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene B</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene W</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #8f3876;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bwy, +++, bwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0771_09dd</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene N</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #8f3876;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jmn, +++, jmn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>669c_691e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276198;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, det, +++, det"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>2e8c_ce0b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #59651b;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #59651b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #59651b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>e27a_6ece</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene A</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #59651b;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #59651b;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #59651b;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, acf, +++, acf"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene B</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1931_e024</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene F</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #8f3876;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #8f3876;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bfr, +++, bfr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9d95_7a99</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #59651b;">Gene E</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #59651b;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #59651b;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276198;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ehp, +++, ehp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>4f85_f41d</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene A</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>4d6b_74c1</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene P</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnp, +++, hnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fa67_6c48</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, nty, +++, nty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene K</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene P</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>03a9_5821</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene H</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hkw, +++, hkw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>d9b7_1aec</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fpy, +++, fpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>18a7_3e1a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene P</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jpy, +++, jpy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>0105_fcaf</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene W</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, wxy, +++, wxy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>ea3f_415c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hwy, +++, hwy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>fa13_0ade</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene D</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene X</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>xenon</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276198;">Gene X</span> cells emit a faint glow under UV light, as if they were fluorescent.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dnx, +++, dnx"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>f143_f571</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene N</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bnp, +++, bnp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene F</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene K</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene J</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjp, +++, cjp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>9ddf_aeae</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene M</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>7064_d3df</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cdp, +++, cdp"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>3b7d_763e</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene T</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hrt, +++, hrt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>8768_9469</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene H</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bdh, +++, bdh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7884_0b6b</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, kry, +++, kry"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>bd58_e636</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene M</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene M</span> colonies are small, dense, and secrete compounds that inhibit the growth of nearby colonies.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene Y</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276198;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cmy, +++, cmy"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene C</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #59651b;">Gene F</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #59651b;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #59651b;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276198;">Gene P</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #276198;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene N</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hnr, +++, hnr"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene A</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene Y</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, aby, +++, aby"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>68d1_5046</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene E</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene K</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #1b6e4d;"><i>knotted</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #1b6e4d;">Gene K</span> cells grow in twisted, coiled shapes, resulting in a knotted or gnarled appearance.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ekw, +++, ekw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7caa_99d8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene H</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene W</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene W</span> colonies produce delicate, web-like strands that connect neighboring colonies in a cobweb pattern.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, hrw, +++, hrw"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>7279_02c9</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, dty, +++, dty"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>03ba_589c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, det, +++, det"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene N</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, npt, +++, npt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene P</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>pebble</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene P</span> produces colonies with a rough, uneven surface that resembles a collection of tiny pebbles.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006788;">Gene R</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006788;"><i>rusty</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006788;">Gene R</span> colonies develop a reddish-brown pigmentation, reminiscent of rusted metal.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene W</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>webbed</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>f319_311a</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, fjt, +++, fjt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene C</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene H</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, ceh, +++, ceh"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>e309_0422</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene J</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #7e540d;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #7e540d;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #006a75;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006a75;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #803a9c;"><i>yolk</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #803a9c;">Gene Y</span> cells develop a dense, yellowish core that resembles an egg yolk when viewed under a microscope.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, jny, +++, jny"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>385b_c2b8</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene C</span></strong> is analogous to the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene J</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene N</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>nude</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene N</span> cells have an unusually smooth surface with no visible external features or textures.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, cjn, +++, cjn"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. MC	<p>6852_8869</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene B</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene E</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>elephant</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene E</span> cells absorb excessive amounts of liquid, resulting in giant, swollen cells.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #983751;">Gene J</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #983751;"><i>jeweled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #983751;">Gene J</span> colonies appear dotted with tiny, iridescent spots that sparkle under light.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, bej, +++, bej"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
