The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene A</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #894c1f;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #894c1f;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene C</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #3753bf;"><i>clumpy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #3753bf;">Gene C</span> grows in dense, irregular clusters, with cells clumping together rather than spreading smoothly.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abc, +++, abc"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #6e5d11;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6e5d11;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene H</span></strong> is affiliated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>hairy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene H</span> cells develop long, thread-like filaments that extend outward, creating a hairy, shaggy texture on the colony.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene T</span></strong> is related to the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. MC	<p>1609_c40c</p> <h5>Unordered Tetrad Three Gene Mapping</h5><p>In this problem, you will use unordered tetrads to determine the between a single pair of genes and calculate the distances between them. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene D</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>doubled</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene D</span> cells display double or multiple budding, with several buds emerging simultaneously.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #006d63;">Gene F</span></strong> is correlated with the '<span style="color: #006d63;"><i>fuzzy</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #006d63;">Gene F</span> colonies are covered in soft, fine filaments, giving them a fuzzy, cotton-like texture.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene M</span></strong> is connected with the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>militant</i></span>' phenotype. The yeast <i>Saccharomyces cerevisiae</i> is used in this study. A cross has been performed to study the linkage relationships among three genes, and the resulting genotypes are summarized in the tables below.</p><h6>Characteristics of Recessive Phenotypes</h6><ul><li><strong><span style="color: #a13321;">Gene A</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #a13321;"><i>amber</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #a13321;">Gene A</span> cells develop a rich yellow-orange pigmentation, giving the colony a warm, amber hue.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span></strong> is associated with the '<span style="color: #276f1b;"><i>bubbly</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #276f1b;">Gene B</span> produces excessive gas bubbles during growth, causing foamy appearance of the media.</li> <li><strong><span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene T</span></strong> is linked with the '<span style="color: #6448ad;"><i>toxic</i></span>' phenotype. A budding yeast that is homozygous recessive for <span style="color: #6448ad;">Gene T</span> secretes a toxic compound that inhibits or kills other microbial colonies nearby.</li> </ul><table style="border-collapse: collapse; color: #202020; background: #ffffff;"><tr><td align="center" style="border: 1px solid #888; padding: 2px;"><svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="156" height="120" viewBox="0 0 122 94" role="img" aria-label="Unordered ascus: +++, abt, +++, abt"><desc>Each recessive allele contributes its own color; plus alleles remain neutral.
